ocr.recognition.v2.description: Submit, observe, cancel, retry, and forget Runtime API v2 OCR jobs.

pdf.edit.v2.description: Open, render, inspect, mutate, stream, and save PDF sessions.

qrcode.v2.description: Decode QR/barcode images and generate QR or SVG image envelopes.

export.document.v1.description: Export OCR content to document formats supported by the Backend.

runtime.settings.v2.description: Inspect residency, preload/release pipelines, and exchange Runtime settings.

runtime.maintenance.v1.description: Observe Runtime Host maintenance over opt-in NDJSON and inspect the authenticated HTTP runtime status snapshot.

task.progress.v1.description: Consume typed units and determinate or indeterminate progress on Runtime jobs and stage events.

runtime.maintenance.v2.description: Use idempotent Runtime maintenance operations, commands, durable sequence cursors, and replay.

runtime.component-repair.v1.description: Inspect desired and actual component drift and request repair by stable component id.

runtime.capability-metadata.v1.description: Negotiate required capabilities and consume lifecycle, deprecation, sunset, and replacement metadata.

runtime.events.sse.v1.description: Replay and follow authenticated Runtime maintenance events as Server-Sent Events after Supervisor readiness.

runtime.events.ndjson.v1.description: Replay and follow authenticated Runtime maintenance events as HTTP NDJSON after Supervisor readiness.

ocr.engine-selection.v1.description: Select the plain-text OCR engine explicitly on job submission and consume the structured engine catalog carried by capability descriptors.

runtime.download-sources.v1.description: Select dependency package indexes and native-engine model-source preferences from the Backend-declared catalog, carried by capability descriptors and exchanged as stable source ids without transferring model-file lifecycle ownership to VibeOCR.

runtime.component-selection.v1.description: Manually select the install scope of optional feature dependencies from the Backend-declared variant catalog, exchanged as install_component_ids with the dependency closure reported honestly.

ocr.recognition-modes.v1.description: Discover user-semantic recognition modes and their exact execution mapping, provisioning, availability, supported options, and honest model-residency or child-process lifecycle capabilities.

ocr.mineru-config.v1.description: Select the typed MinerU 4 tier, OCR mode, canonical page range and language on mineru_parse jobs, negotiated against the Backend-declared tier and language catalog carried by capability descriptors.

ocr.mineru-remote-api.v1.description: Configure a self-hosted MinerU 4 V1 parsing service through SettingsSnapshot.extra.mineru_connection without installing local MinerU dependencies or models; retain local mode and never fall back from a failed remote request to local execution.

runtime.install-plan.v1.description: Preview a read-only Runtime install plan for ensure over runtime.maintenance.v2, runtime.component-selection.v1 and runtime.download-sources.v1: requested and effective component/source closures, retain/install/replace/remove actions with machine reason codes, honest blockers with next actions, deduplicated cost totals and expiry, confirmed later via plan_id on maintenance start or retry without installing, downloading, or changing any active environment.

ocr.default-recognition-mode.v1.description: Persist the instance-wide default recognition mode id through SettingsSnapshot.extra.default_recognition_mode and read the resolved committed default back from GET /v2/settings. A missing key keeps the legacy default rapid_text. Exchanges validate the value type and catalog id on every write, and availability only when the default changes, so a stale stored default never blocks unrelated settings updates. Invalid snapshots are rejected without replacing prior settings. Clients MUST NOT send the key to runtimes lacking this capability. Explicit per-job mode overrides keep precedence, submitted jobs keep their submit-time parameters, and saving the default never installs components or changes any environment.
